en.title: Bad Bunny & Alan Cumming Join Toy Story 5 as Iconic New Characters
en.summary: The beloved Pixar franchise is set to welcome two unexpected, yet delightful, additions to its voice cast. Global music superstar Bad Bunny and acclaimed actor Alan Cumming are lending their talents to key new roles in the highly anticipated Toy Story 5.
en.body:
The world of Andy's toys is about to get a lot more interesting. With **Toy Story 5** officially on the horizon, set for release in 2026, Pixar has been steadily revealing details that have fans buzzing. The latest news comes in the form of two high-profile voice cameos that promise to add unique flavor and star power to the enduring franchise: global music phenomenon **Bad Bunny** and the versatile actor **Alan Cumming**.

For over two decades, the **Toy Story** saga has captured hearts by exploring the emotional lives of toys, always grounded in themes of friendship, belonging, and the bittersweet nature of growing up. From Woody's unwavering loyalty to Buzz Lightyear's existential crisis, each installment has deepened our connection to these characters. Now, as Bonnie navigates her own childhood and the evolving landscape of play, the toys face a new challenge, and the introduction of fresh faces, especially those voiced by such distinctive personalities, signals an exciting new chapter.

## A Battle for Playtime

The narrative core of **Toy Story 5**, as hinted at by the recently released final trailer, centers on a conflict between Bonnie's cherished toys and a new piece of technology: a "Lilypad" screen. This device, reminiscent of early 2011 tablet computers, aims to monopolize Bonnie's attention, threatening to sideline her traditional toys. Leading the charge against this digital usurper is none other than **Jessie**, the spirited yodeling cowgirl, who rallies the gang to reclaim their playtime with Bonnie. This premise taps into contemporary anxieties about screen time and its impact on childhood imagination, a theme that resonates deeply in our increasingly digital world.

The emergence of new allies and adversaries is a hallmark of any **Toy Story** adventure, and this time, the roster is set to be particularly star-studded. Pixar has officially announced that **Bad Bunny**, the six-time Grammy Award winner and global superstar, will voice a character named "Pizza with Sunglasses." Described as "effortlessly cool and mysterious," this character is part of a "small but mighty community of forgotten toys" residing in an abandoned backyard shed. One can only imagine the charisma and effortless cool that **Bad Bunny** will bring to this unique toy.

Equally exciting is the addition of **Alan Cumming**, a celebrated actor known for his diverse roles across film, television, and theater. Cumming will lend his distinctive voice to "Evil Bullseye." While the specifics of Bullseye's turn to the dark side are still under wraps, the mere mention of an "Evil Bullseye" conjures images of a delightfully menacing, yet perhaps ultimately redeemable, antagonist. This casting choice is particularly intriguing, given Bullseye's established history as Woody's loyal, if somewhat simple, horse companion. The prospect of a sinister version, voiced by Cumming, promises a compelling new dynamic for the toys.

## Fan Frenzy and Forgotten Friends

The announcement of **Bad Bunny** and **Alan Cumming** joining the **Toy Story 5** ensemble has predictably sent waves of excitement through the fandom. Fans have long appreciated Pixar's ability to blend heartfelt storytelling with unexpected casting choices, and this pairing is no exception. The idea of **Bad Bunny**, an artist celebrated for his boundary-pushing music and undeniable swagger, voicing a cool, forgotten toy speaks to the franchise's enduring appeal to diverse audiences. Similarly, **Alan Cumming's** reputation for bringing complex and captivating characters to life makes "Evil Bullseye" a figure fans are eager to meet.

Beyond the star power, the concept of "forgotten toys" and the battle against a monopolizing screen taps into a deeper emotional chord. It speaks to the enduring value of physical play, imagination, and the unique bonds formed with cherished objects in an era dominated by digital interactions. The introduction of these new characters, particularly those from the "forgotten toys" community, suggests a potential exploration of themes around obsolescence, memory, and the importance of preserving the magic of childhood play. This resonates with the core audience who grew up with **Toy Story** and now share its magic with their own children.

## What's Next

As **Toy Story 5** continues to shape up for its 2026 release, the focus will undoubtedly remain on how these new elements integrate into the beloved world we know. The introduction of **Bad Bunny** as Pizza with Sunglasses and **Alan Cumming** as Evil Bullseye are more than just star cameos; they represent Pixar's continued commitment to pushing creative boundaries and surprising its audience. With the final trailer setting the stage for a significant conflict, fans can anticipate a story that is both a nostalgic return and a fresh adventure, exploring new dimensions of what it means to be a toy in the 21st century.

Toy Story 5 Features Bad Bunny as Pizza & Alan Cumming as Evil Bullseye We also have a final Toy Story 5 trailer, where Jessie leads the fight against the screens By Vanessa Armstrong | Published on May 26, 2026 Credit: Disney/Pixar Comment 0 Share New Share Toy Story 5 Features Bad Bunny as Pizza & Alan Cumming as Evil Bullseye&url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Toy Story 5 Features Bad Bunny as Pizza & Alan Cumming as Evil Bullseye” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Credit: Disney/Pixar The fifth Toy Story movie is almost upon us, and it’s set up to be a battle between the toys and a smartass Lilypad screen. The young human, Bonnie, still plays with Jessie, Forky, and her other toys, but she soon gets a newfangled device called a Lilypad (think of the LeapPad tablets circa 2011 in our timeline ) that says that Bonnie is ALL HERS ALL OF THE TIME. Jessie, as the final trailer released today makes clear, isn’t standing for it. She leads the other toys in a battle against the screen for playtime with Bonnie. The toys she meets along the way are a mix of old characters and new… and today Pixar announced two additional guest cameos that fill me with joy. The first cameo is Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio, who you may know as six-time Grammy Award winner Bad Bunny. He is lending his voice to the soon-to-be iconic character, Pizza with Sunglasses. What kind of character is PWS, as I’m calling him? His official description describes him as “effortlessly cool and mysterious” and a member of “a small but mighty community of forgotten toys that live in an abandoned backyard shed.” Ey! The second cameo is also delightful! Alan Cumming’s dulcet voice will also appear in the film as Evil Bullseye. Bullseye, Toy Story fans know, is Woody’s loyal, non-talking horse. Cumming’s evil version of the toy is reportedly quite loquacious, which we’ll see (and hear) during one scene of the film. We won’t have to wait long to see these cameos in the fifth film in the franchise: Tickets are now on sale for Toy Story 5 , which premieres in theaters on June 19, 2026. While you wait, check out the final trailer below. [end-mark] The post Ey! Toy Story 5 Features Bad Bunny as Pizza & Alan Cumming as Evil Bullseye appeared first on Reactor .
